summary.headline: Third-party compliance, Remote Help, and endpoint-management guidance receive a broad refresh
summary.overview: The day records 86 changes, led by device-compliance partner guidance and new endpoint-management services documentation, with accompanying Remote Help, Autopilot, and Configuration Manager maintenance.
summary.adminImpact: Organizations that rely on third-party compliance partners should validate their connector and Conditional Access runbooks against the refreshed documentation. Use the new endpoint-management overview as a current orientation reference; no broad policy migration is indicated.

keyChanges.title: Third-party device compliance partner guidance is updated
keyChanges.detail: The refreshed partner-support reference remains the operating source for integrating partner device-compliance signals with Intune.

keyChanges.title: Endpoint management services overview is added
keyChanges.detail: A new fundamentals article provides a consolidated orientation to Microsoft endpoint-management services and solutions.

summary.headline: Privacy governance and Zero Trust deployment guidance define the final February week
summary.overview: The week records 250 changes, centered on a new privacy, data-sharing, and regulatory-alignment documentation set; a Zero Trust deployment approach; and supporting Configuration Manager diagnostic, Autopilot, Remote Help, and compliance-partner updates.
summary.adminImpact: Update privacy and regulatory evidence packs from the new data-flow documentation, use the Zero Trust plan to coordinate security workstreams, and refresh 2509 diagnostic-data and Autopilot workflow runbooks. Verify third-party compliance-partner processes before relying on them in Conditional Access decisions.

keyChanges.title: Privacy and data-sharing guidance is rebuilt
keyChanges.detail: New documentation explains Intune data security, collection, storage, secure sharing, personal-data rights, and data exchanges with Apple, Google, Zebra, and Jamf.

keyChanges.title: Zero Trust deployment approach is published
keyChanges.detail: New planning guidance establishes an Intune-centric reference for sequencing Zero Trust deployment and security configuration.

keyChanges.title: Configuration Manager 2509 diagnostic guidance is added
keyChanges.detail: A new reference updates the support and governance material for diagnostic and usage-data collection in Configuration Manager 2509.

summary.headline: February sharpened Intune operational governance, reporting quality, and policy foundations
summary.overview: February recorded 675 changes and three Message Center announcements. It consolidated Apple profile guidance, refreshed RBAC and endpoint-security references, added a major privacy and governance documentation set, clarified Cloud PKI CA continuity, and announced reporting treatment for devices inactive at least 12 months.
summary.adminImpact: Prioritize updating privacy and regulatory documentation, Apple configuration runbooks, and custom-role audits. Set expectations for reporting-count changes in late February, preserve Cloud PKI CA replacement readiness, and use the refreshed Endpoint security and Autopilot guidance as support baselines.

keyChanges.title: Endpoint security guidance is extensively refreshed
keyChanges.detail: The core Intune device-protection reference receives a substantial revision and remains the foundation for endpoint-security policy design.

keyChanges.title: Inactive devices are excluded from Intune reporting
keyChanges.detail: Beginning in late February, reports exclude devices inactive for 12 months or more, improving active-fleet accuracy while potentially lowering reported counts.

keyChanges.title: Privacy and regulatory documentation is reorganized
keyChanges.detail: A broad new documentation set provides current descriptions of Intune data handling, secure sharing, partner data flows, and compliance alignment.

summary.headline: Zero Trust, Remote Help, licensing, and Security Copilot references receive a broad March refresh
summary.overview: The first March update day records 115 changes, led by Zero Trust security, Remote Help planning, licensing, Intune Suite add-ons, and the Change Review Agent documentation.
summary.adminImpact: Use the refreshed Zero Trust and Remote Help planning pages when updating operating models. Evaluate Security Copilot Change Review Agent guidance before assigning responsibility for automated change review, and validate add-on licensing before enabling related capabilities.

keyChanges.title: Zero Trust security guidance is updated
keyChanges.detail: The Zero Trust configuration guide receives a major revision and remains the primary source for Intune security planning.

keyChanges.title: Remote Help planning guidance is refreshed
keyChanges.detail: The Remote Help plan reference is updated, providing current information for support-service design and rollout planning.

keyChanges.title: Change Review Agent reference is updated
keyChanges.detail: Security Copilot’s Change Review Agent documentation is revised as part of the March support and automation refresh.

summary.headline: February service update is announced as Managed Home Screen and device-location guidance is refreshed
summary.overview: The day includes February Intune service-update announcement alongside updates to in-development content, device location, and Managed Home Screen OEMConfig permissions.
summary.adminImpact: Check Tenant Status and What’s New for the February build, then review upcoming features with help desk and product owners. Use the current Managed Home Screen permission documentation before changing frontline-device OEMConfig policies.

keyChanges.title: February 2026 Intune service update is announced
keyChanges.detail: The Message Center post confirms the February service build and directs administrators to Tenant Status and What’s New for feature and readiness detail.

keyChanges.title: Managed Home Screen OEMConfig permissions guidance is updated
keyChanges.detail: The Android Enterprise Managed Home Screen permission reference is refreshed, keeping the current configuration guidance available for frontline-device administrators.
